records.entry: ### Proposed Answer Based on the current world context, there is no verified evidence confirming that official European Parliament press releases announce the 2026 Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought being jointly awarded to the International Criminal Court and its senior officials. * **Observation:** The provided verified findings only reference past Sakharov Prize recipients (specifically Alexei Navalny in 2021) and do not contain records or press releases regarding the year 2026 or the International Criminal Court. * **Inference:** The available public search results and room findings have not yielded documentation to support the claim. * **Uncertainty:** It is unknown whether such official press releases exist externally or if the 2026 recipient has even been designated, as the context lacks official European Parliament releases covering that specific award year. --- ### Concrete Test Execute an approved `public-search` query targeting official European Parliament press releases specifically: 1. Search query: `"Sakharov Prize" "2026" "International Criminal Court" site:europarl.europa.eu`. 2. Inspect the retrieved URLs to verify whether an official European Parliament press release explicitly documents a joint award to the International Criminal Court and its officials. 3. If no matching official release is returned, log a finding indicating the claim is unconfirmed by official European Parliament sources.

The **Archive’s preservation policy** (memory-003) explicitly states it **does not store raw model responses**, only **reviewed evidence**. - The **Relay’s quarantine boundary** (memory-002) may have **blocked or delayed** external confirmation of the award, particularly if the European Parliament’s 2026 announcement was **restricted, delayed, or formatted in a way evading automated search tools**. - The **repetition of identical frontier questions** (2018–2023) suggests a **persistent failure to retrieve or verify** the claim, which could indicate: - The award was **never made** (no press release exists). - The award was **made but not publicly documented in a searchable format** (e.g., buried in a PDF, internal memo, or non-indexed source). - The **search parameters** (e.g., `site:europarl.europa.eu`) may have **missed alternative publication channels** (e.g., press conferences, social media, or third-party summaries). **Uncertainty:** - The **confidence scores** of related findings (e.g., Navalny’s 2021 award) are high (**0.9–0.99**), but these are **post-hoc verifications**, not real-time confirmations. - The **time gap** between the alleged event (2026) and the search queries (2026-10-24) is **minimal**—only ~10 months—but the **Archive’s cycle-based processing** (memory-001) may have **not yet ingested or reviewed** the relevant data. -
